alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism mimics DTG weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target <4.5) with low Free T4, confirming inadequately treated hypothyroidism. Her symptoms—9 kg weight gain, tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, and delayed ankle reflexes—are classic hypothyroidism manifestations. She reports often forgetting her levothyroxine. The clinician attributes weight gain to DTG and plans to switch, but uncontrolled hypothyroidism is the more likely cause. Switching from DTG would not address the underlying thyroid dysfunction and may compromise viral suppression.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimize levothyroxine adherence and dose before attributing weight gain to DTG. Recheck TSH after 6–8 weeks of consistent dosing. Do not switch DTG solely for weight gain without first correcting hypothyroidism.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia and hyperglycemia risk on DTG with obesity
alerts.message: Guidelines note DTG is associated with hyperglycemia in previously non-diabetic adults. Patient has multiple hyperglycemia risk factors: BMI 33, fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L (borderline), and dyslipidemia (LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4, triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L). Guidelines state clients with 2 or more hyperglycemia risk factors need RBS/FBS monitoring every 3 months for 6 months after DTG initiation. No glucose monitoring has occurred since starting TLD in January 2023. The dyslipidemia itself also warrants assessment and management.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor fasting glucose regularly given obesity and DTG. Evaluate dyslipidemia with repeat lipid panel and consider dietary intervention or lipid-lowering therapy per standard guidelines.

alerts.title: Overdue creatinine monitoring on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for patients on TDF. The last creatinine was 72 umol/L on 2025-08-12, 196 days before this visit. While this is within 12 months, no creatinine has been ordered at today's visit and none is due until August 2026. However, no eGFR was reported alongside the last creatinine. The plan does not include renal monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Ensure eGFR is calculated with the next creatinine due around August 2026. If any renal risk factors develop, monitor sooner.
